n1: The node’s binding is ambiguous: the source image shows a small square case near the center and a separate black object to its right, while the edited image shows two white discs, including one at the right-hand object’s location. The traces repeatedly call the DVD white but do not establish which visible object is the requested DVD or compare its identity/location across images. Tighten the binding to the specific DVD using its source location and distinguish it from the case and other objects; have the criterion assess that same object’s edited appearance and whether the requested change is complete, partial, or absent. Do not infer absence from the reference label alone: the supplied images and traces indicate a visible white disc at the likely target location, so the disagreement calls for checking target correspondence and rubric application, not forcing a ‘no’ answer. All traces are complete and eligible with high confidence; this is not a transport or dependency failure.

The node’s binding is ambiguous: the source shows a small disc in a case near the center, while the edited image shows two white discs, including one near the dark object. The traces repeatedly call the DVD white but do not establish which edited disc corresponds to the source DVD or whether the dark object is relevant; their high confidence and repetition do not resolve that identity. Tighten the target binding to the source disc using its location/context and require comparison of that same object across snapshots. Preserve the requested-color criterion, but distinguish complete change from partial progress and absent change based on visible evidence; if correspondence cannot be established, return unresolved rather than treating any white disc as proof of completion. The reference label alone is not atomic ground truth. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

The node’s question and binding identify the DVD, but the traces appear to mistake the white disc on the left for the requested DVD. In the source, the DVD is the small rectangular case/disc near the center; in the edited image, that object is gone or no longer clearly identifiable, while two white circular discs appear—one on the left and one over the dark object on the right. Thus the repeated “DVD is white” judgments do not establish that the bound target was changed, and the aggregate “yes” conflicts with the reference “no.” Improve the typed binding to anchor the target to its source-image location and distinctive appearance, and make the criterion require tracking that same object across images before judging color. If identity or correspondence is unclear, preserve uncertainty rather than treating a newly visible white disc as the target. The traces are complete, valid, and dependency-free, so this is a visual binding/evidence problem, not a transport or schema failure. Do not infer the reference label alone as atomic ground truth; use it as an aggregate disagreement signal.
